newsitem.title: UK: European holidays, U.S. data slow down Eurobonds.
newsitem.headline: European holidays, U.S. data slow down Eurobonds.

text.p: The Eurobond market was subdued on Friday after a hectic week due to holidays in much of Europe and in anticipation of October U.S. jobs data due for release later.
Dealers said the figures would be closely watched.
A Reuter poll of economists showed an average forecast of a 212,000 gain in October non-farm payrolls, compared with September's 40,000 fall.
The only new issue to surface was a $150 million one-year FRN from Bank of Melbourne, which paid three-month Libor flat and was launched at par.
Looking ahead, there were few deals in the pipeline.

Mexico was due to issue a 500 billion lire five-year FRN next Thursday via Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, the country's first transaction in lira and the first floating lira deal from an emerging market borrower.
There was some uncertainty surrounding the launch spread of the deal, which some traders said would be in the high-200s b.p. over swaps.
Later, others said the low to mid-200s b.p. over was more likely and this spread was in line with where outstanding Latin American debt was trading.
The lead manager was not available for comment.
In dollars, Korea Development Bank was expected to issue a $500 million global bond via J.P. Morgan and Merrill Lynch.
The French franc sector, which saw a surge of 10-year deals this week, was likely to remain active next week, dealers said.
More German banks could tap the sector, and U.S. agency Fannie Mae was also said to be eyeing the 10-year maturity.
